newsitem.title: UK: Firm overseas markets support thin Euro veg oils.
newsitem.headline: Firm overseas markets support thin Euro veg oils.

text.p: Firm futures markets in Asia and the U.S. supported prices at midday on Thursday on a thin European vegetable oil market.
Palm oil players were mostly sidelined following a further rise in prices in Malaysia, despite the lack of export business.
"The Malaysia market is up on technical factors, there is no fundamental reason for the rise, just the opposite in fact," said a trader.
Traders said palm oil output is coming into its peak production months with no sign of major buyers coming into the market for volume business.
Crude palm oil cif Europe was up $7.50 to $5 at midday with some early business reported in June at $545 and $547.50 a tonne cif.
In products RBD palm oil was $2.50 up to unchanged while olein was $5 to $2.50 higher after Jul traded at $570 and Jul/Sep at $565 a tonne fob Malaysian ports.
Soft oils were fully steady with soy and rape oil 2.50 to two guilders higher but with no business reported so far.
Traders said coconut oil players were walking on egg-shells after Wednesday's shake-out.
"Most people are keeping out of the way until they see whether the U.S. players will be in again this afternoon," said one.
Sellers at midday were $5 up to unchanged while palmkernel oil was $5 down to unchanged.
